idea: astra 2026-11-20 idea #1 (executable disproofs): select code by executable contracts that can refute candidates even when they agree.
question: Does arbiter-free executable-disproof selection close part of the coding selection gap (first-passing vs oracle) without any hidden information?
dataset: datasets/coding-hard-v1 evaluation split (24 tasks x seeds 1-3 = 72 cases)
contract_model: Inkling-2-Mini (the fleet model; INKLING serving + inkling/shim.py), one contract per case from the PUBLIC task only; thinking on, budget 12288 first call / 16000 total with forcing; seeds 66000+index
contract_validity: loads in the pinned CPU sandbox, >=1 input of the right arity, check() exactly True on every public example
disproof: check() exactly False on any (contract input, candidate output value); exceptions/timeouts/non-bool never disprove
selection_rule: earliest non-disproved feedback-passing candidate; fallback to earliest feedback-passing (original rule) if contract invalid, no passing candidate, or all disproved

candidate_sets.inkling: runs/inkling-coding-hard-v1 (8 Inkling agents per case): primary, same model writes contracts and code
candidate_sets.nemotron: coding-hard-xl-v1 + v1b + ext-v1 (8 Nemotron agents per case): secondary, cross-model contracts

outcomes: solved/72 at k=4 and k=8 vs first-passing and oracle; wrong and correct candidates disproved
scheduling: contracts run alongside the two Inkling runs with 1 request per node (summed client concurrency 25)
source_note: selection is frozen in selections.json before holdout results are read; holdout results are those already recorded by each coding run
